issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition officer lacks authority to allot acquired land in lieu of monetary compensation under the statutory award-making and compensation-payment powers.
material_facts: Land was acquired for a public purpose.
In a later award, the acquisition officer deducted the value of plots allotted to the landowners in lieu of compensation.
The landowners sought to enforce the allotment of acquired land as part of the award.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition officer had no power to allot the acquired land in lieu of compensation. The limited power under Section 31(3) to arrange for other land applied only to a person with a limited interest in the acquired land and required prior government sanction; Section 31(4) did not enlarge that power.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 11 and 18 confine the acquisition officer’s award and the reference court’s inquiry to matters such as the area acquired, compensation, and its apportionment. Section 31(3) permits, with the appropriate government’s sanction, an arrangement involving other land in exchange for compensation only for a person having a limited interest in the acquired land. Section 31(4) preserves the power to make arrangements with a person competent to contract but does not authorize allotment of acquired land in lieu of compensation. The acquisition scheme, including Sections 4, 6, 16 and 48, does not permit the officer to create a right to reclaim part of acquired land in a way that defeats the public purpose. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land and the determination or payment of compensation for it.
predicates.acquired_land_allotted_instead_of_money: The acquisition officer allotted land that was itself acquired rather than paying monetary compensation for the acquired interest.

issues.definition: When a compensation proceeding involves allotment of the acquired land instead of money, the acquisition officer lacks authority to make that allotment.

issues.legal_issue: A decree or award directing delivery of acquired land outside the matters authorized for determination in acquisition proceedings may be challenged as a nullity during execution.
material_facts: The civil court on reference confirmed the acquisition officer’s award, subject to correcting certain deductions.
The award included a direction for allotment of land in lieu of compensation, and the landowners sought delivery of that land in execution.
The acquiring authority objected in execution that the allotment was beyond the officer’s jurisdiction; the High Court held that the objection could not be raised at that stage.
issues.conclusion: The allotment direction was a nullity and could be challenged in execution. The execution proceedings seeking delivery of land under that direction were invalid, void and inexecutable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 18 and 26(2), the reference court determines the referred statutory questions, and its award is a decree only to the extent of matters properly determined under the acquisition law. A decree cannot make executable a direction that the acquisition officer lacked jurisdiction to give. The invalidity or nullity of such a decree may be raised during execution. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_execution_proceeding: A party is seeking execution of a decree or award arising from land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.decree_directs_delivery_of_acquired_land: The decree or award directs delivery of acquired land as an allotment in lieu of compensation.

issues.definition: If execution proceedings seek enforcement of a decree directing delivery of acquired land, the delivery direction may be challenged in execution and is inexecutable.

issues.legal_issue: A court will not direct allotment of alternative land on the basis of an asserted government policy when the policy is not produced and the circumstances do not otherwise support specific directions.
material_facts: A request was made for directions to allot suitable alternative sites under an asserted government policy.
The policy was not brought to the court’s notice.
It was stated that allotments to other persons were disputed in pending appeals and that no one had received the benefit of those awards.
issues.conclusion: The court declined to issue specific directions for allotment of alternative sites.
issues.legal_principle: The court gave no specific direction because the asserted policy was not placed before it and the status of other allotments was disputed in pending appeals. No earlier cases or statutory provisions are cited for this decision.

predicates.appellate_land_acquisition_proceeding: The court is considering an appeal arising from land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.alternative_allotment_policy_not_produce: A party relies on a government policy for alternative land allotment but does not place that policy before the court.

issues.definition: In an appeal arising from land acquisition proceedings, when the relied-on alternative-allotment policy is not produced, the court does not issue a specific direction for alternative land.
